en.greeting: Hi, welcome back! Today we learn small but very useful words: I, you, he, she, it, we, they, and my, your, his, her. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Words that replace names
steps.text: Let's start with the words we use instead of a name.
steps.body: A **pronoun** is a short word used instead of a name. A **subject pronoun** replaces the person or thing doing something, at the start of a sentence (*Rina* → **she**). Indonesian 'dia' becomes **he** for a man or boy and **she** for a woman or girl. Things and animals are **it**. More than one person or thing is **they**. **we** is both 'kami' and 'kita', and **you** is one person or many.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Think about the person first. Man or woman?

question.prompt: Complete: Bu Sinta is our new teacher. ___ is from Medan.
question.explanation: Bu Sinta is a woman, so we use **she**. **He** is only for a man or boy, and **it** is for things and animals.

steps.title: Whose is it? my, your, his, her
steps.text: Now let's show who owns something.
steps.body: Use a **possessive** to show the owner. It goes **before** the noun (the person, thing or place): **my bag**, not 'bag my', though Indonesian says 'tas saya'. Choose by the **owner**, not the thing: Budi (a man) → **his** mother; Sari (a woman) → **her** father. Indonesian '-nya' doesn't show this.

steps.title: Possessives in sentences
steps.text: Look where the possessive sits: always right before the thing.
steps.body: The owner word comes first, then the noun: **my** phone, **her** office.

examples.en: This is my phone.
His name is Andi.
Her office is on the second floor.
Our teacher is kind.
Their house is near the market.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A word comes before a noun here. Which form do you need?

question.prompt: Complete: Pak Hasan is my neighbour. ___ car is white.
question.explanation: Before a noun (car) we need a possessive, not **he**. Pak Hasan is a man, so it is **his**, not **her**: we look at the owner.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Put the words in English order. Remember: owner first, then the thing.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kamar (room) mereka besar (big).
question.explanation: In English the possessive comes before the noun: **Their room**, then **is big**. Indonesian 'kamar mereka' puts the owner last, English puts it first.

steps.title: Don't repeat the noun
steps.text: Once you name someone or something, you can switch to a pronoun.
steps.body: After you say the noun once, use a pronoun: one man → **he**, one woman → **she**, one thing → **it**, more than one → **they**, you and me → **we**.

examples.en: The laptop is new. It is fast.
Bu Rina is in a meeting. She is busy.
examples.id: Bu Rina sedang rapat. Dia (perempuan) sibuk.

examples.en: My parents are at home. They are happy.
examples.id: Orang tua saya di rumah. Mereka senang.

examples.en: Andi and I are friends. We play futsal.
examples.id: Andi dan saya berteman. Kami main futsal.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Who is in the first sentence? Count the people.

question.prompt: Complete: My mother and I are at the market. ___ need rice.
question.explanation: 'My mother and I' means another person plus me, so the pronoun is **we**. **They** does not include you, and **I** is only one person.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards and say the meaning before you check.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here is a cheat sheet you can keep and look back at.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Personal pronouns
artifact.intro: Subject pronouns start the sentence. Possessives show the owner and go before the noun.
tips: Picture the person before you speak: man → **he / his**, woman → **she / her**.
The possessive goes **before** the noun: **my bag**, not 'bag my'.
Name it once, then switch to a pronoun: one thing → **it**, many → **they**.
**his / her** follow the owner, not the thing: Budi → **his** mother, Sari → **her** father.

examples.en: She is in a meeting.
His car is red.
Our house is small.
The phone is new. It is black.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? These short videos and a reference page help.

id.greeting: Hai, selamat datang kembali! Hari ini kita belajar kata-kata kecil tapi sangat berguna: I, you, he, she, it, we, they, serta my, your, his, her. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Kata pengganti nama
steps.text: Kita mulai dari kata yang dipakai untuk menggantikan nama.
steps.body: **Kata ganti** adalah kata pendek pengganti nama. **Kata ganti subjek** menggantikan orang atau benda yang melakukan sesuatu, di awal kalimat (*Rina* → **she**). 'Dia' dalam bahasa Indonesia menjadi **he** untuk laki-laki dan **she** untuk perempuan. Benda dan hewan memakai **it**. Lebih dari satu orang atau benda memakai **they**. **we** berarti 'kami' sekaligus 'kita', dan **you** untuk satu orang atau banyak.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bayangkan orangnya dulu. Laki-laki atau perempuan?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Sinta is our new teacher. ___ is from Medan.
question.explanation: Bu Sinta perempuan, jadi pakai **she**. **He** hanya untuk laki-laki, dan **it** untuk benda dan hewan.

steps.title: Milik siapa? my, your, his, her
steps.text: Sekarang kita tunjukkan siapa pemilik sesuatu.
steps.body: Pakai **kata kepemilikan** untuk menunjukkan pemilik. Letaknya **sebelum** kata benda (orang, benda atau tempat): **my bag**, bukan 'bag my', walaupun bahasa Indonesia bilang 'tas saya'. Pilih berdasarkan **pemiliknya**, bukan bendanya: Budi (laki-laki) → **his** mother; Sari (perempuan) → **her** father. '-nya' dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak membedakan ini.

steps.title: Kata kepemilikan dalam kalimat
steps.text: Perhatikan posisinya: selalu tepat sebelum bendanya.
steps.body: Pemilik dulu, baru kata bendanya: **my** phone, **her** office.

examples.en: This is my phone.
His name is Andi.
Her office is on the second floor.
Our teacher is kind.
Their house is near the market.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Di sini ada kata sebelum kata benda. Bentuk mana yang kamu perlukan?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Pak Hasan is my neighbour. ___ car is white.
question.explanation: Sebelum kata benda (car) dibutuhkan kata kepemilikan, bukan **he**. Pak Hasan laki-laki, jadi **his**, bukan **her**: yang dilihat adalah pemiliknya.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Susun kata-katanya dalam urutan bahasa Inggris. Ingat: pemilik dulu, baru bendanya.

question.explanation: Dalam bahasa Inggris kata kepemilikan ada sebelum kata benda: **Their room**, lalu **is big**. 'Kamar mereka' menaruh pemilik di belakang, bahasa Inggris di depan.

steps.title: Jangan ulang kata bendanya
steps.text: Setelah menyebut seseorang atau sesuatu, kamu bisa ganti dengan kata ganti.
steps.body: Setelah kata benda disebut sekali, pakai kata ganti: satu laki-laki → **he**, satu perempuan → **she**, satu benda → **it**, lebih dari satu → **they**, kamu dan saya → **we**.

examples.en: The laptop is new. It is fast.
Bu Rina is in a meeting. She is busy.
examples.id: Bu Rina sedang rapat. Dia (perempuan) sibuk.

examples.en: My parents are at home. They are happy.
examples.id: Orang tua saya di rumah. Mereka senang.

examples.en: Andi and I are friends. We play futsal.
examples.id: Andi dan saya berteman. Kami main futsal.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Siapa saja di kalimat pertama? Hitung orangnya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: My mother and I are at the market. ___ need rice.
question.explanation: 'My mother and I' artinya orang lain ditambah saya, jadi kata gantinya **we** (kami). **They** tidak termasuk dirimu, dan **I** hanya satu orang.

steps.title: Ulang cepat
steps.text: Balik kartunya dan sebutkan artinya sebelum kamu cek.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini ringkasan yang bisa kamu simpan dan buka lagi kapan saja.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Kata ganti orang
artifact.intro: Kata ganti subjek ada di awal kalimat. Kata kepemilikan menunjukkan pemilik dan ada sebelum kata benda.
tips: Bayangkan orangnya sebelum bicara: laki-laki → **he / his**, perempuan → **she / her**.
Kata kepemilikan ada **sebelum** kata benda: **my bag**, bukan 'bag my'.
Sebut sekali, lalu ganti dengan kata ganti: satu benda → **it**, banyak → **they**.
**his / her** mengikuti pemiliknya, bukan bendanya: Budi → **his** mother, Sari → **her** father.

examples.en: She is in a meeting.
His car is red.
Our house is small.
The phone is new. It is black.
